findings.text: the configured window reaches the surface only where a caller passes the full backend mapping; the recorded-row readers reconstruct the backend from argv and drop it — dispatch._backend_settings returns {'launch':'cli','command':argv[0]} whenever a run records argv (dispatch.py:3678), recovery.py:485 and :712 build {'command': ...}, and promotion.py:1302 observes through _backend_settings(record, None), so the fold/resume/recovery/promotion surfaces still divide input_utilisation_pct by the client's announced stream window, the exact behaviour the plan forbids; only the live probe (budget.py:1380 -> probe_lane_availability -> observe_log with the configured settings mapping) actually pins to the window that enforces the budget — the reviewed seam is correct but no test asserts a caller passes the window, so the announced-window denominator at the plan's own evidence surfaces (committed rows reading peak/200000) is unchanged at HEAD.

the manifest's armed after_suite block names command 'tests/test_budget.py' and total 64 while the attached after_suite.log reads '112 passed in 6.00s' — the parsed total does not match the log the manifest points at; the 64 figure is independently reproducible for test_budget.py at the head (a separate run), so the delta claim holds, but the recorded attribution contradicts the attached log and an automated reader taking total from the block would record the wrong pairing.

justifications.durability: The guard is real and fires — the five tests exercise the genuine observe_log path with real JSONL, the conflict case asserts refusal rather than arithmetic, the (0,1) ratio case is satisfied by nothing short of the refusal, and every expected percentage is computed from fixture constants at assertion time so nothing freezes a moving figure; docked because the guard sits only at the dialect seam: the durable verdict rows the plan names are folded through callers that drop the configured window, and no test pins a caller passing it, so a caller regression that re-opens the announced-window denominator on recorded rows would go uncaught.
justifications.evidence: The headline claims reproduce — the gate passes 5/5 at the reviewed head 47a3180, the five-file fence suite passes 112, and test_budget.py passes 64 at the head against a 64 baseline at a76cb93 whose code carries no pinning and no test file, so the change adds guard plus tests with zero added failures; docked because the armed after_suite block's total contradicts its attached log, and because no test says any production caller hands the configured window to the seam, leaving the caller half of the fix unattested.
justifications.fit: The change follows the established idiom and stays mechanism-named — observe gains one keyword, _throughput resolves precedence through a small pure _resolved_window helper whose provenance string feeds the detail clause, and the codex dialect accepts-and-ignores with a documented reason (codex streams do not declare a configured window through this path); docked because the fix assumes callers pass the backend mapping, which the argv-reconstruction paths contradict, so the wiring stops at the seam and cannot reach the fold surface without touching callers outside the reviewed fence.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The done-when is met and reproduced (5 passed: announced-only names its window beside the figure; a configured lane window defeats an announced conflict asserted equal to the configured value and never the midpoint nor the announced one; no window resolves to unknown, never a constant; a (0,1) ratio is refused; whole-number percentages parse), so the dialect-level consequence is implemented well; docked because the configured window reaches the surface only via the probe path (budget.py:1380 passes the full settings mapping), while the recorded-row readers the plan's own evidence cites reconstruct the backend from argv and drop it — those surfaces still divide by the announced window at HEAD, which the plan's consequence says must never happen.
justifications.scope_discipline: The node wrote exactly its two declared write paths (reckon/_backends.py, tests/test_utilisation_names_its_window.py) in one conventional commit 47a3180 with subject and body, verified the base bacc7f7 is reached with delta 0, kept the worktree clean at the committed head, and under the LANDING-vs-rule conflict correctly followed binding rule #4 and the prior node's precedent — code landed and outcome data returned rather than editing plan state in scope.
